# Paul Irving

## Overview

- **Age:** 16  <sub>[v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c28 P23](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0023)</sub>
- **Origin:** The States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P83](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0083)</sub>
- **Role:** Poet  <sub>[v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033), [v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Uncle Paul  <sub>[v5 c3 P14](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0014)</sub>

## Appearance

By age sixteen, Paul is a tall, handsome youth standing six feet tall, having grown rapidly from a small child. He has dark blue eyes and close-cropped brown hair that was once a halo of chestnut curls. In his childhood, he possessed a delicate, refined face with a grave, thoughtful expression that illuminated warmly whenever he smiled.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c15 P11](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0011), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Paul is an imaginative, sensitive, and highly gifted individual with a deep, poetic soul and occasional flashes of uncanny insight. Despite his dreamy, sensitive nature and rich inner life, he is manly, clean, fair-minded, and polite, holding his own well in sports and among his peers. He possesses a strong sense of devotion and loyalty to those he loves.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P7](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0007), [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P32](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0032), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c23 P36](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0036), [v2 c27 P54](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0054), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006)_

## History

Paul Irving came from Boston to Avonlea to live with his grandmother on the shore road after the death of his mother. At the Avonlea school, he quickly formed a deep bond with his teacher, Anne Shirley, who recognized his poetic genius and became his close confidante. As a child, he fought a drawn battle with schoolmate St. Clair Donnell to defend the American flag and nurtured childhood crushes while enjoying imaginative stories about "rock people" and "dream-people." He later met Miss Lavendar Lewis, who eventually married his father, Stephen Irving, giving Paul a loving stepmother whom he called "Mother Lavendar." After his father and stepmother relocated to Boston, Paul eventually joined them, growing into a tall young man interested in football and literature. He successfully published a volume of poetry and drove the carriage for Anne and Gilbert Blythe on their wedding day. Later, he embarked on a two-year period of study abroad in Europe, remaining an inspirational model of poetry for Anne's son Walter.

## Quotes

> Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I’m going to need all my strength of mind to bear up against this, Grandma, and I won’t have any left to grapple with porridge. Oh Grandma, I don’t know what I’ll do when my beautiful teacher goes away.  <sub>[v2 c26 P35](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0035)</sub>

> You see, that name belongs just to my own little mother, and I can’t give it to any one else. You know, teacher. But I call her ‘Mother Lavendar’ and I love her next best to father.  <sub>[v3 c23 P4](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0004)</sub>

> You’ll never grow old, Teacher. You are one of the fortunate mortals who have found and drunk from the Fountain of Youth,—you and Mother Lavendar.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
